examples.question_text: A bird population varies between a maximum of $1400$ and a minimum of $800$, repeating every $12$ months. The population is greatest when monitoring begins. Find the amplitude, mean position and constants in $P(t)=k\cos(at)+c$, where $t$ is the number of months since monitoring began.

At midnight a bay has a low tide of $0.8$ m. The next high tide, at $6{:}15$ am, is $5.2$ m. Find $k$, $a$ and $c$ in $h(t)=k\cos(at)+c$, where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight, and write the model.

An alternating voltage ranges from $-180$ V to $180$ V and completes $40$ cycles each second. The voltage is zero and rising at $t=0$. Find the period and a model $V(t)=k\sin(at)+c$, with $t$ in seconds.

coverage.summary: Added a vertical-axis break below the 800 tick in example 0, matching the supplied population sketch. examples.derivation: A=(1400−800)/2=300, c=(1400+800)/2=1100 and a=2π/12=π/6. The initial maximum requires k=300. P(t)=300cos(πt/6)+1100 gives P(0)=P(12)=1400 and P(6)=800, matching the plotted cycle and truncated vertical scale.

6:15 am is 6.25 hours after midnight, so T=12.5 hours. A=(5.2−0.8)/2=2.2, c=(5.2+0.8)/2=3 and a=2π/12.5=4π/25. The initial minimum requires k=−2.2. The model gives h(0)=h(12.5)=0.8 and h(6.25)=5.2, matching the sketch.

A=(180−(−180))/2=180, c=0, T=1/40 second and a=2π/(1/40)=80π. Starting at zero and rising requires V(t)=180sin(80πt). Its maximum occurs at 1/160 second and minimum at 3/160 second. The plot maps four horizontal coordinate units to 1/40 second, consistently placing both extrema and the labelled half-period.
